title: He didn’t fall overnight.
paragraphs:
He didn’t fall overnight.
He drifted… quietly.
And that’s what should terrify you.

Because Demas didn’t start as a traitor.
He started as a worker in the Gospel.
His name was once spoken in the same breath as faithful men (Colossians 4:14, Philemon 1:24).
But something happened in the silence.

Something no one applauded.
Something no one posted.
Something no one confronted.
Until it was too late.
Paul writes it like a wound you can feel: “Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted me” (2 Timothy 4:10).
Read that again.

Not attacked.
Not persecuted.
Not confused.
In love… with this present world.
That’s the open door.
That’s the quiet killer.

Because you don’t have to hate Jesus to leave Him.
You just have to love something else more.
And here’s the part most people won’t say out loud:

You can preach…
and still be drifting.

You can lead…
and still be losing your first love.

You can post Scripture…
and still be secretly negotiating with sin.
Let me ask you something that might sting—
When did Jesus stop being enough for you?

Was it when the prayers felt unanswered?
When obedience became inconvenient?
When the world started offering you what God was asking you to wait for?
Here’s the hidden struggle nobody admits:
Delayed obedience.

Not rebellion.
Just… postponement.

“I’ll surrender later.”
“I’ll deal with this sin eventually.”
“I’ll go deeper… when life calms down.”
But Scripture doesn’t say Demas woke up one day and ran.
It says he loved the world.
Meaning his heart slowly shifted before his feet ever moved.
AHA REVELATION:

You don’t walk away from God in your steps first—
you walk away in your affections.
And once your love changes… your direction follows.

Jesus warned us about this kind of drift.
In Matthew 24:12, He said “because lawlessness will increase, the love of many will grow cold.”
Not explode.
Grow… cold.
Gradually. Quietly. Dangerously.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

If your passion for God is fading while your appetite for the world is increasing…
you are not “going through a phase.”
You are drifting.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.

Some of you aren’t far from God in position…
you’re far from Him in affection.

You still attend.
Still serve.
Still look the part.

But if we’re honest—
your heart is somewhere else.
And here’s the piercing truth:
God doesn’t just see your actions—He weighs your loves.
Jesus said the greatest commandment is not performance… but love (Matthew 22:37).
So what happens when your love shifts?

You become like Demas—
close in proximity…
but distant in devotion.
And religion will never confront that.

Religion will clap for your activity
while your heart quietly abandons Christ.
That’s the danger.
That’s the deception.
That’s why this matters.
But listen carefully—
Demas is a warning.
Not a sentence.

Because the same Bible that exposes drift
also offers rescue.
Here’s the Gospel:

You and I have loved the world more than we should.
We’ve chosen comfort over calling.
We’ve delayed obedience.
We’ve entertained sin.

That’s not small.
That’s sin.
And sin separates us from God (Isaiah 59:2).
But God did not respond by walking away from us.
He came closer.
Jesus Christ stepped into our drift.

He lived the perfect life we couldn’t live,
and died the death we deserved on the cross.
Not for the strong.
For the wanderers.
For the compromised.
For the ones who knew better… and still chose lesser.
Romans 5:8 says “while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

That includes your slow drift.
Your hidden compromise.
Your divided heart.
And here’s the hope that changes everything:
You can come back.
Right now.

Not when you feel worthy.
Not when you’ve fixed everything.
Now.
Because repentance is not God pushing you away.
It’s God pulling you back.

The cross is not just for your past sins—
it’s for your present drift.
IDENTITY SHIFT:
You are not called to be a believer who almost stayed.
You are called to be a lover of Christ who endures to the end (Matthew 24:13).
You are not defined by how you started.
You are marked by Who you choose daily.
So here’s the invitation—

Come back before distance becomes departure.
Come back before affection becomes abandonment.
Fall in love with Jesus again.

Not casually.
Not halfway.
Fully.
If this is hitting your heart… don’t ignore it.
Step into that if you’re serious about growing.
And if you feel this conviction…
Because next, we’re going deeper into the signs you’re drifting before you even realize it.
